The Ideal Profile We are looking for an inspiring educational leader who combines academic rigor, strong interpersonal skills, and a commitment to Africa’s development. One team of 21,000 colleagues that's energising a greener, fairer future by creating an energy system that doesn’t rely on fossil fuels, whilst living our powerful commitment to igniting positive change in our communities. Here, you can find more purpose, more passion, and more potential. That’s why working here is #MoreThanACareer. We do energy differently - we do it all. We make it, store it, move it, sell it, and mend it. At Centrica, we're not just adapting to the future of energy, we're shaping it – and we’re looking for curious minds, fresh perspectives and ambitious graduates to help us make it happen. As an Engineering Graduate , you'll have the opportunity to work on meaningful projects, solve real business challenges and make an impact from day one. You'll gain hands-on experience, develop the critical skills needed for your future career and build a network that will support you throughout your journey. Why Engineering? As one of the UK's largest integrated energy companies, our engineers play a critical role in developing, operating, upgrading and transforming the infrastructure and technologies that will power the energy transition. Our Engineering Graduate Programme offers the opportunity to build experience across a diverse portfolio of assets, projects and technologies, spanning areas such as nuclear, power generation, energy storage, hydrogen, heat networks and other emerging energy solutions. Through a combination of technical and business placements, you'll develop the skills, experience and professional network needed to build a successful engineering career while helping shape a more sustainable energy future. Along the way, you'll develop skills in engineering design, asset management, project delivery, risk management, stakeholder engagement and problem solving. You'll gain exposure to the technical, operational and commercial challenges involved in delivering safe, reliable and sustainable energy solutions at scale. Through a combination of hands-on experience, structured development and diverse placements, you'll build the technical expertise, professional capability and commercial awareness needed to become a future engineering leader at Centrica. Support to help you thrive We're looking for potential, not perfection. That's why you'll be supported every step of the way through structured development opportunities, experienced mentors and line managers, dedicated graduate learning, buddy support and a network of graduates from across the business. With offices across the UK and a hybrid approach to working, flexibility is an important part of our graduate programmes. You’ll need to be open to travel when required and, for some placements, relocation, giving you the opportunity to experience different teams, locations and parts of our business. Click here To Explore The Full Job Description. What we need from you: Expecting a First Class Degree in a suitable engineering discipline, accredited by the relevant engineering institution (or a 2:1 with Masters Degree) Degrees may include Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Process Engineering, Nuclear Engineering, Energy Engineering, Energy Systems Engineering, Renewable Energy Engineering, or a closely related engineering subject Curious, proactive and keen to learn Willingness to travel and relocate between placements where required Right to work in the UK A full UK driving licence or working towards obtaining one by September 2027 Available to start in September 2027 Here’s what's in it for you: Starting salary of £36,000 per annum You’ll be eligible for our annual bonus scheme and a profit-based share incentive plan A three-year programme, featuring three rotational placements across different areas across Engineering Structured support and development throughout the programme Opportunities to learn from experienced professionals and build your network A chance to make a meaningful contribution while developing skills that will support your future career Why should you apply? We’re not a perfect place – but we’re a people place. Our priority is supporting all of the different realities our people face. Life is about so much more than work. We get it. That’s why we’ve designed our total rewards to give you the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, making sure that you and your family are supported not only financially, but physically and emotionally too. Visit the link below to discover why we’re a great place to work and what being part of more means for you. https://www.morethanacareer.energy/centrica If you're full of energy, fired up about sustainability, and ready to craft not only a better tomorrow, but a better you, then come and find your purpose in a team where your voice matters, your growth is non-negotiable, and your ambitions are our priority. Help us, help you. We would love for you to share any information about yourself throughout our recruitment process so that we can better understand you and help shape your journey.

review_candidates.title: Finance and Support Services Director
review_candidates.description: With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith. Come join our 33,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories! Here’s where you come in: As Finance and Support Services Director , you will provide overall leadership, oversight, and management support for all aspects of financial management in the Field Office (FO). You will serve as a strategic partner and member of the Senior Leadership Team (SLT) of WV Mauritania, focusing on accountability, stewardship, planning and budgeting, accurate financial data and analysis, and financial advice. You will develop a financial strategy that supports the Field Office’s strategic and programme objectives. You will also strengthen finance staff capacity, develop and implement effective internal controls and risk management practices, and ensure the proper utilization and safeguarding of assets in accordance with World Vision-approved policies and procedures. (a) Leadership, Capacity Development, and Strategic Partnering You will provide strong and positive leadership to the Finance Department, ensuring competent and motivated staff are recruited and retained to deliver efficient services. You will coordinate the professional and personal development of Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff through orientation, on-the-job coaching, training, and succession planning. You will model Christ-centred servant leadership and support your team’s spiritual development. You will actively participate in Field Office Senior Leadership Team meetings and strategic regional meetings, help the National Director (ND), Operations, and other non-finance staff understand financial statements, and ensure relevant stakeholders understand partnership finance policies and procedures. You will strengthen collaboration and communication between the Field Office and Regional Office, develop internal and external networks, promote shared resources across the region and partnership, and adhere to WVI’s mission, core values, and Covenant of Partnership. (b) Stewardship You will ensure that appropriate cost-efficiency and effectiveness measures are implemented and followed. You will provide cost analyses, promote benchmarking, and make recommendations to improve resource utilization at all levels. In collaboration with the Supply Chain team, you will contribute to developing appropriate policies and procedures for procuring goods and services. (c) Financial Planning and Budgeting In collaboration with the Regional Finance Director, you will advise the National Director on strategic resource acquisition and allocation in line with Partnership Resource Allocation Committee (PRAC) guidelines. You will coordinate planning and budgeting processes, provide technical support to ensure compliance with global and regional guidelines, and develop and implement financial strategies in response to changing constraints and circumstances. You will review budget alignment across the Field Office, projects, grants, MyPBAS, and Support Offices, ensuring effective cost recovery practices. In collaboration with the Integrated Programs Director (IPD), you will monitor and manage the WV Mauritania budget, cash flow, and project funding, providing timely and relevant information to budget managers. You will closely monitor budgets and expenditures at Area Development Program (ADP), Cluster, and Field Office levels to ensure funds are used for their intended purposes, including monitoring field expenses. You will also contribute to developing WV Mauritania’s strategic direction and priorities. (d) Fiscal Accounting, Compliance, Monitoring, and Reporting You will design and manage systems, policies, and procedures that provide appropriate security and control over WV assets, resources, and operations. You will establish effective internal controls and ensure timely, accurate, and complete reporting to the partnership and internal stakeholders. You will comply with partnership policies, procedures, and guidelines outlined in the WVI Financial Manual and related documents, including grant compliance, planning and budgeting, year-end closing, carryforward, accounting, and reporting. You will coordinate the timely and accurate submission of financial reports through the Field Financial Reporting database on SharePoint, review monthly MyPBAS-to-FFR reconciliations, and develop action plans to address outstanding items. You will provide monthly analyses of ADP and grant financial reports, giving timely feedback to ADP and grant managers to support decision-making. You will also ensure that Finance, ICT, Fleet, and Administration staff visit programmes and projects to monitor accountability, follow up on audit findings, and provide necessary support. (e) Financial Risk Management and Controls You will manage appropriate financial systems and controls to minimize significant finance audit risks at both Field Office and project levels. You will coordinate management responses to financial audits, ensure timely submission to the Audit Department, and oversee the timely implementation of audit recommendations. You will coordinate adequate preparation for Global Centre (GC) and external audits, manage financial risks and integrity, and implement anti-corruption and fraud prevention strategies. (f) Support to Supply Chain Processes You will coordinate and maintain an effective interface between the Supply Chain and Finance teams. You will review Purchase Requests and Purchase Orders to ensure compliance with Supply Chain Management (SCM) policies, budget availability, and appropriate controls against fraudulent activities. You will also review procurement activities to ensure purchases contribute to ministry objectives and align with donor budget line items. (g) Improve ICT Infrastructure and Provide Quality Service You will ensure improved connectivity across the office and programmes and facilitate the development and implementation of computer usage policies. You will oversee ICT security and integrity, ensuring office disaster preparedness measures and policies are regularly updated to address new technologies, trends, and threats. (h) Administration and Fleet Management You will ensure that WV staff and assets remain secure, safe, and well-maintained, while overseeing logistics coordination and providing quality hospitality services to staff and visitors. You will implement fleet management policies covering vehicle tracking, fuel management, and vehicle and motorcycle maintenance. You will also manage asset disposals in compliance with WVI and WV Mauritania policies. (i) Talent Management and Capacity Building You will contribute to capacity assessment, development, and implementation as part of the overall Talent Management Plan, ensuring an integrated WV Mauritania capacity-building plan informed by finance priorities and strategy. You will identify Finance staff development needs, including grant financial management, and facilitate relevant training opportunities while developing diverse leadership. In collaboration with the People and Culture (P&C) Team Leader, you will co-lead the recruitment of Field Office Finance staff. You will advise and support the induction of new functional directors, grant managers, and project team leaders. You will also coach, advise, and mentor Finance staff to identify their strengths and development gaps and address them effectively. Requirements include: Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, or Economics or a related field Minimum 5 years of experience in a finance position with a medium business/medium NGO/government agency Minimum 3 years of experience in a senior finance management position Experience with financial planning and forecasting Solid knowledge of accounting principles, financial systems, budget/cash flow monitoring, and internal accounting controls. Highly flexible and agile in style, with the ability to produce creative and pragmatic solutions to complex problems. Good working knowledge of computerized accounting systems, preferably Sun Systems & ProVision. Demonstrates systems thinking and is a high champion and Manages Innovation. Able to work in a cross-cultural environment with a multi-national staff. Ability to travel within the country, regionally, and internationally. French is non-negotiable (both written and spoken) Proficiency in written and spoken English Excellent oral/written and interpersonal skills Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA's) Accepted Is this the job for you? Find the full responsibilities and requirements for this position and apply online by the closing date October 20, 2026. World Vision is dedicated to our team members’ development and their success. We aspire for all employees to be fulfilled through their work and their contributions to an organisation working to provide long-term sustainable solutions to the world’s most vulnerable people. For more information on World Vision International, please visit our website: www.wvi.org.Our vision for every child, life in all its fullness. Our prayer for every heart, the will to make it so.

review_candidates.title: Engineering Manager
review_candidates.description: Healthcare is in crisis and the people behind the results deserve better. With more and more data coming from wearables, lab tests, and patient–doctor interactions, we’re entering an era where data is abundant. Junction is building the infrastructure layer for diagnostic healthcare, making patient data accessible, actionable, and automated across labs and devices. Our mission is simple but ambitious: use health data to unlock unprecedented insight into human health and disease. If you're passionate about how technology can supercharge healthcare, you’ll fit right in. Backed by Creandum, Point Nine, 20VC, YC , and leading angels, we’re working to solve one of the biggest challenges of our time: making healthcare personalized, proactive, and affordable. We’re already connecting millions and scaling fast. Short on time? You: You’ve led experienced engineers, stayed close to the code, and care about the product and the customers using it. Ownership / Focus: You’ll lead a small and growing engineering team, you’ll own its engineering direction, technical delivery, team health and hiring. How we manage: We don’t believe in purely pastoral engineering managers. You’ll manage and develop people, but you’ll also ship, unblock, review and make technical decisions alongside them. Salary: £120-£150k + equity (based on experience and location) Location: Fully remote (GMT). We have one company offsite each year, with possible travel to London every couple of months for team meet-ups. Why we need you Our engineering team is growing, and we need another Engineering Manager to grow with it. You’ll report to Mark, our Head of Engineering, and work alongside Rui, our other Engineering Manager. You’ll initially take ownership of a small engineering team, working closely with product and other teams to decide what to build and get it shipped. At Junction, engineering management is a technical job. We want our managers close enough to the work to know what’s going on, give good feedback and get involved when needed. But we don’t want you to become the person everyone waits for when something gets difficult. Six months in, your team should trust you, people outside the team should know where things stand, and the team should be delivering what it says it will. What You’ll Be Doing Day To Day Own the engineering direction, delivery and health of a small team of senior product engineers. Work with product on what the team commits to, then make sure it gets delivered. Stay close to the code: review PRs, give technical feedback, pair on problems and ship when it makes sense. Unblock the team when decisions are unclear or things go wrong. Give engineers regular feedback, run useful 1:1s and performance reviews, and actively help them grow in their careers. Notice what’s slowing the team down and fix it, surface problems early and keep the rest of the company clear on what’s happening. Own hiring for your team and play an active role in helping Junction grow. Requirements You’ve led and directly managed experienced software engineers. You’ve stayed technically involved while managing You’ve owned a team’s delivery, not just its people management. You can give useful technical feedback and make sound calls on engineering trade-offs. You’ve worked with product and other teams to turn customer problems into shipped software. You’ve helped engineers develop through direct feedback, coaching and meaningful opportunities to take on more. You’ve hired engineers and helped raise the technical or operating standards of a team. You don’t need to tick every box to fit in here. If the problems we’re solving genuinely interest you and you know you can contribute, we’d love to talk. Nice to have You’ve worked at an early-stage or scaling company where managers are expected to manage people and build product. What This Role Isn’t If you want to stay out of the code and spend most of your time in 1:1s, planning and status meetings, it won’t be a good fit. You’ll have to make tough calls on technical and non-technical topics and own the outcomes It isn’t a tech lead role with a few 1:1s either. Developing people, giving difficult feedback, hiring and building a healthy team are core parts of the job. How You'll Be Compensated Your salary is dependent on your location and experience level Equity (extended exercise post 2 years of employment) Company and team offsites Monthly learning budget of $150 for personal development and productivity $100 monthly wellness budget Flexible, remote-first working, including $1K for home office equipment Coworking budget 36 days paid time off (including bank holidays) Premium healthcare coverage 4% monthly contribution to pension/401k Yearly blood test on us Enhanced parental, foster, and adoption leave Important details before applying: We only hire folks physically based in GMT and EST timezones We do not sponsor visas right now given our stage Compensation Range: £120K - £150K

review_candidates.title: Director, Key Accounts
review_candidates.description: Imagine having the power to stress-test an entire power grid against a hurricane or thunderstorm before the clouds even gather. That is the reality we are creating at Neara. We use advanced machine learning to create engineering-grade, physics enabled digital twins of electricity grids across four continents, this helps asset owners understand their biggest challenges and bring the most viable solutions to life across millions of kilometres of infrastructure. By simulating extreme weather and structural stress at a network-wide scale, we empower the world’s largest utilities to pinpoint risks, optimise investments and build a more resilient global energy future. Our team is a collection of brilliant minds who are fanatical about making a tangible difference in the real world, utilising AI and machine learning to accelerate everything from data classification to complex scenario analysis. We have built a special culture where innovation thrives because everyone owns the mission and we need smart, creative people to help us scale this impact to every corner of the globe. Director, Key Accounts We're seeking a driven, dynamic, and strategic commercial leader to drive growth across our key accounts in Europe. This is a hands-on, high-impact player-coach role focused predominantly on personal account execution paired with informal team leadership and commercial mentoring. To succeed in this role, you will need a consultative mindset, excellent communication skills, and knowledge of the utilities industry. You will also need a proven track record of commercial execution across large, multi-year, multi-faceted contracts, and experience leading or mentoring a customer-facing team. What You'll Do Personally own and grow relationships with a portfolio of our most strategic accounts, serving as the senior commercial relationship owner and executive point of contact. Develop and deliver expansion plans across assigned key accounts to execute against business metrics and revenue goals. Coach the team on account strategy, executive engagement, and commercial execution on complex, multi-year contracts. Identify new workflow improvements and use-case opportunities, helping to upskill the broader customer-facing team in commercial best practices. Collaborate with Customer Success Operations, Customer Value Architects, and Product on overall account strategy and execution. Develop processes to scale the Key Account Management function as Neara's European business grows. Co-present with utilities at key conferences and events across Europe, helping elevate Neara’s market presence. Report on account performance, pipeline, and expansion opportunities to senior leadership. Who You Are Demonstrated history of personally managing and expanding enterprise-level accounts within complex technical or SaaS environments, ideally operating as a Director of Key Accounts, Director of Sales, Key Account Manager, Client Partner, or in a similar enterprise role. Domain exposure to the utilities sector or a similarly complex, technical, infrastructure-heavy industry is highly desirable. Experience leading, managing, or mentoring Account Managers or Customer Success Managers, ideally in a player-coach capacity. Experience in strategic sales, management consulting, or tech-enabled enterprise environments. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to navigate executive dynamics and foster a collaborative, customer-centric culture internally. Fluent in English (required); additional European languages are a plus. What We Are Offering You Competitive salary + commission structure. Significant development opportunities with scope for lateral and upward movement in a high-growth company. Highly meritocratic, non-bureaucratic, and low-ego work culture. The opportunity to play a direct, critical role in expanding Neara’s footprint across Europe’s largest utilities to solve real-world infrastructure problems. Enjoy the opportunity to work across multiple business areas and build relationships with key internal and external stakeholders.
